Exit

엑시트 (Eksiteu)

K-Drama · Movie · South Korea · 2019

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐∞/10

Overview

Exit follows Lee Yong-nam, a jobless young man who once excelled at rock climbing during college. He still lives with his parents and is constantly reminded by his family that he needs to get his life together. During his mother's 70th birthday celebration at the Cloud Garden, Yong-nam unexpectedly reunites with his former college crush and fellow rock climber, Eui-joo, who now works at the venue. However, their reunion takes a terrifying turn when a mysterious toxic white gas is released throughout the city. With the gas rapidly spreading and people desperately trying to escape, Yong-nam and Eui-joo are forced to use their old climbing skills, improvisation, teamwork, and determination to survive. Their journey takes them across rooftops, buildings, cranes, and dangerous gaps as they desperately search for a way to escape the rising gas. What starts as an ordinary family birthday celebration turns into a fight for survival.

My Review

I already watched this way back in 2020, I think, and it was such a good movie. Highly recommended! I cried a lot while watching this. 🥹 There are still kind people in this world who are willing to put others before themselves, and I really loved how that was shown in this movie. The story was really good. Honestly, no explanation is needed—it was one of the best movies I've watched. Yes, it doesn't have a crazy plot twist, but the thrill was enough. Shit. 😭 Especially for someone who's afraid of heights, this movie was kind of challenging to watch. There were so many scenes where they were climbing buildings, jumping between rooftops, hanging from ropes, and going across really high places. I'm actually proud of myself because I realized that I'm not as afraid of heights as I thought I was. 😂 Maybe I wasn't really that afraid before. After rewatching it, I still cried a lot. Hehehe. It was just too good. I really loved the determination of both Yong-nam and Eui-joo. They didn't just think about themselves. They kept trying to survive while also helping other people along the way. There were moments when they could have chosen themselves, but they still decided to help others first. That's probably one of the things I loved most about this movie—the characters weren't superheroes. They were just ordinary people trying to survive an extraordinary situation, but they showed so much courage. I also loved Yong-nam and Eui-joo's relationship. 😭 The fact that Yong-nam had confessed to Eui-joo before and got rejected about four years earlier, and then they met again during this crazy disaster, was actually funny and cute. Like... imagine getting rejected by your crush years ago and then the next time you meet, you're both literally trying to escape toxic gas by climbing buildings together. 😭 I just wished the ending had given us a little glimpse of them actually dating or getting married. HAHAHAHA. I wanted at least a small confirmation that they ended up together. But honestly, it was still good. Very, very good. Their determination to survive was amazing. They kept going even when they were exhausted, scared, and had almost no options left. And that's why Exit became a comfort movie for me. It has action, comedy, disaster, survival, family, friendship, and a little romance. It's thrilling without being unnecessarily complicated, and even though I've already watched it before, the movie still made me feel the same emotions when I rewatched it. I cried again. 😭 I especially loved how the movie showed that sometimes ordinary people can become incredibly brave when the people they love are in danger. There were also moments where people helped each other despite being strangers, which made the story even more meaningful to me. The movie doesn't need an insane plot twist to be good. The thrill, determination, emotional moments, humor, and survival scenes already made it memorable.

Favorite Scene/Part

• Yong-nam and Eui-joo climbing and crossing the buildings together. This was probably one of the favorite parts because it perfectly showed their determination. They're exhausted, the toxic gas is getting closer, they're surrounded by dangerous heights, and they still have to keep moving. • Another favorite moment was when they redirected the rescue opportunity toward the trapped students instead of choosing to save themselves first.

Favorite Quote/Lines

"Keep going, even when there seems to be no way out."
